title: Acceleration and Its Sign
short: a = Δv/Δt; an object slows down when its acceleration points opposite to its velocity.
trouble: Students think negative acceleration always means slowing down.

blocks.html: In Acceleration acceleration was how quickly velocity changes. Now velocities carry signs, so acceleration does too, and its sign holds a surprise.

$\role{acceleration}{a} = \dfrac{\role[change in velocity]{velocity}{\Delta v}}{\role[time interval]{time}{\Delta t}} = \dfrac{\role[final velocity]{velocity}{v_f} - \role[initial velocity]{velocity}{v_i}}{\role[time interval]{time}{\Delta t}}$. An object speeds up when $a$ and $v$ point the same way and slows down when they point opposite ways. The sign of $a$ alone doesn't tell you which.

Acceleration points in the direction of the change in velocity. A car moving in the $-x$ direction at $-10\ \text{m/s}$ that speeds up to $-16\ \text{m/s}$ has a change of $-6\ \text{m/s}$: its acceleration is negative and it is speeding up. "Negative" is a direction on your axis, not a word for "slowing".

blocks.title: Speeding up in the minus direction
blocks.q: A bus heading west speeds up from $10\ \text{m/s}$ to $16\ \text{m/s}$ in $3\ \text{s}$. Take east as $+x$.
steps: Heading west, both velocities are negative: $v_i = -10\ \text{m/s}$, $v_f = -16\ \text{m/s}$.
Negative acceleration, and the bus is speeding up, because $a$ and $v$ are both negative.

blocks.title: Through a turnaround
blocks.q: A ball rolls up a ramp at $+6\ \text{m/s}$. Five seconds later it rolls down at $-4\ \text{m/s}$. Find its acceleration.
steps: The ball slowed, stopped for an instant and sped up the other way, with the same acceleration the whole time.

blocks.html: Thinking a negative acceleration always means slowing down. It means slowing down only when the velocity is positive. Check by comparing directions: draw the $v$ arrow and the $a$ arrow. Same way, speeding up; opposite ways, slowing down. The word "deceleration" is fine in everyday talk, but in a problem always write $a$ with its sign.
